strengths: The migration ladder (php/lib/store.php:234-344) is the right shape for every schema change below: SCHEMA_VERSION + migrateStep(), each step under BEGIN IMMEDIATE, hasColumn() guards (store.php:531-539) making ALTER TABLE idempotent, and practice-test.php:93 pinning the version so a forgotten bump fails CI.

Practice ingest is already a general telemetry channel: metrics_schema is advisory (practice.php:24-29, mcp.php:1709-1725), so any new NUMERIC per-session measure stores today with no deploy, and every panel type can plot metrics.<key> (practice.php:153-159, 262-263). This is the lever most of the ADHD features can pull immediately.

tracker_set_scoreboard validates the whole configuration and refuses unknown keys (practice.php:176-294), and stored configs are appended not replaced (store.php:1426-1433), so board experiments are reversible and cannot half-apply.

The golden-snapshot discipline (deploy/practice-test.php:468-532, tests/golden/*) protects the one screen the student is known to care about; the maths snapshot is built from the MATHS_SCOREBOARD constant, so production board edits via the tool never touch it.

Every page is server-rendered with zero JavaScript (grep '<script' over php/ finds nothing; picker documented as working with JS off at practice.php:1237-1240), charts repeat their numbers as a table (practice.php:653-669), and the whole site is one stylesheet (dashboard.php:20-120), so a new student page is cheap and consistent.

The audit trail is sound: sessions stamp every change (store.php:691-725, mcp.php:1273-1282), voids keep rows (store.php:996-1017, 1310-1317), duplicate practice runs are no-ops (store.php:1164-1235). New session fields can ride on this without a second write path.

The review queue already returns resources indented under each topic (mcp.php:926-937) and closes with the last session's next_steps (mcp.php:982-989), so a 'next three things' view has a natural source.

Tests are real and fast: smoke-test.sh walks OAuth + all 21 tools (SMOKE PASS locally), practice-test.php runs 124 checks; ci.yml runs both on every PR and deploy.yml re-verifies production read-only after each merge.

findings.evidence_needed: Self-monitoring of error types and visible progress feedback improve accuracy and engagement for students with ADHD (metacognitive/self-monitoring interventions); time-on-task recording as a basis for session-length decisions.

In updateTopicStatus accept optional 'recall' => 'pass'|'fail': pass -> recall_streak+1, interval_days = RECALL_INTERVALS[min(streak, 5)], next_due = last_touched + interval; fail -> streak 0, interval 1, next_due = +1 day; any transition to secure with no recall seeds next_due = +3 days. findings.evidence_needed: Spacing effect and expanding retrieval practice in secondary mathematics; whether spacing effects hold for learners with ADHD.

findings.evidence_needed: Worked examples and short instructional video for novices in mathematics; reducing task-initiation barriers for ADHD by pre-selecting materials.

findings.title: A chunk clock without JavaScript: what the no-JS constraint allows
findings.where: php/lib/dashboard.php:20-120 (DASH_CSS), :122-130 (dash_shell emits no script); php/index.php:311-318 (route pattern to copy); deploy/smoke-test.sh:94-113 (page checks); README.md line 196 and practice.php:1237-1240 (JS-off is a stated property)
findings.problem: No page has a timer, and adding one with JavaScript would be the first script tag in the service (none exist; the picker's documentation treats JS-off as a feature). The constraint is real but narrower than 'no timer': it rules out pause/resume, sound and per-second logic, not a visible clock.
findings.why_it_matters: Time blindness is a core ADHD difficulty; a visible chunk (25 minutes, then a break) externalises time and matches the tutor skill's own 10/30/30/10 session shape, which currently exists only as prose in a chat window.
findings.proposal:
Add ?chunk=25 handling to the today page (finding 2) and, if wanted, a bare /s/{slug}/timer route. Allowed by the constraint, in order of robustness: (1) a CSS keyframe bar:
with .chunk i{animation:chunk calc(var(--mins)*60s) linear forwards} @keyframes chunk{from{width:100%}to{width:0}} under @media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference); (2) so the page itself flips to 'Break — 5 minutes' at the end of the chunk; (3) server-rendered fixed text 'Started 16:05 · chunk ends 16:30' computed in Europe/London from a ?start= parameter; (4) a ticking mm:ss via CSS @property --t + counter-reset + content: counter(), which works in current Chromium, Safari and Firefox 128+ and degrades to the bar elsewhere. Not possible without JS: pause/resume, persistence across reload except via the URL, sound. The tutor skill links 'open /s/maths/today?chunk=25' at the start of a shape-A session. Tests: smoke contains 'class="chunk"' on the page, and add a global check that no page contains '
findings.evidence_needed: External time cues and chunked work intervals for ADHD time perception; break scheduling effects on sustained attention in adolescents.

The JSON API exists for scheduled jobs but only accepts OAuth bearer tokens issued through the consent flow, so an external cron cannot call it without going through the browser handshake; there is no mail configuration and no cron in the deploy.
findings.why_it_matters: The parent oversees sessions intermittently; a weekly view that names the habits trend, what moved, what is due and the next deadline lets them intervene on pacing rather than on content, without reading every session.
findings.proposal: 1) Page /s/{slug}/week (and /week for all subjects) in dashboard.php: sessions this ISO week with duration and ending (finding 5), topic changes from history($slug, 1), attempts since Monday, practice attempted and flag sums over 7d (practice_window_runs), 'due next week' from finding 3's schedule, and 'coming up' from finding 9. No schema. 2) Delivery with no deploy: a weekly Claude Routine (fresh session, Monday 07:00 Europe/London) that calls tracker_history(weeks:1), tracker_practice_stats(days:7), tracker_list_attempts and tracker_review_queue and writes a five-line digest with the /week link; this needs no service change at all. 3) Email from the service is the expensive option: a CLI script php/cron/digest.php guarded by define('TRACKER', true), PHP mail() or an SMTP secret, and a DreamHost cron entry that ship.sh does not manage; do it only if the Routine proves insufficient. Tests: smoke detail pages: /s/maths/week returns 200 and contains 'This week'. Effort: page about 3.5 h; Routine about 1 h; email about 4 h plus manual server setup.
findings.evidence_needed: Parent-involvement and home-school communication effects for adolescents with ADHD; whether weekly summaries change parental support behaviour.

findings.title: What every service change above will break unless updated: tool count, schema-version pin, source-registry list, golden snapshots, seed reach
findings.where: deploy/smoke-test.sh:261-283 (tool loop and '[ "$tools" -eq 21 ]'), :279-283; deploy/practice-test.php:93 (schema_version === '3'), :94-96 (exact source key list), :468-532 (golden diff and pinned assertions); php/lib/practice.php:68-81 (MATHS_SCOREBOARD is the snapshot input), :30-39 (PRACTICE_SOURCE_SEED applied only in step 3, store.php:328-330); php/lib/store.php:234-262 (ladder), :531-539 (hasColumn), :745-755 (counts for /healthz); php/lib/seed.php:21-25; .github/workflows/ci.yml:26-34; .github/workflows/deploy.yml:43-50, 105-106
findings.problem: Five tripwires are easy to miss. (a) Any new tracker_* tool fails smoke-test.sh:279-283 until the count 21 is changed and the description leads with USE WHEN. (b) Any SCHEMA_VERSION bump fails practice-test.php:93 until the literal '3' becomes '4'. (c) Any new practice source fails the exact-array check at practice-test.php:94-96. (d) Any edit to MATHS_SCOREBOARD or SPANISH_SCOREBOARD constants, or to a render function in practice.php, changes tests/golden/* and fails CI until practice-test.php --update is run and the diff read; editing the stored production config via tracker_set_scoreboard does not. (e) Constants such as PRACTICE_SOURCE_SEED and seed.php are not re-applied to the production database: step 3 has run and seedIfEmpty sees subjects, so new metric keys or resources need either a migration step that re-upserts or a tool call.
findings.why_it_matters: A red deploy blocks every feature behind it, and a migration that works on a fresh database but not on production risks the only copy of the record; knowing the tripwires up front is what makes the small changes above small.
findings.proposal: Adopt a per-change checklist in gcse-tracker-dashboard SKILL.md 'Changing what the dashboard shows' (lines 112-136): new tool -> update smoke count, README table, tracker-service.md; schema -> new migrateStep with hasColumn guards, bump SCHEMA_VERSION and practice-test.php:93, add any new table to Store::counts() and a /healthz assertion like smoke-test.sh:88-92; constants that must reach production -> re-upsert inside the new step (upsertPracticeSource is ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE, store.php:1141-1144, so it is idempotent); panel/render changes -> run practice-test.php, read the diff, --update deliberately. Also fix the stale text 'current 15 tools' in five skill files (there are 21). Prove each migration against a copy of production: sqlite3 .backup as in DEPLOYMENT.md:187-191, open it with a throwaway .env, run it twice to show the second run is a no-op. Effort about 1 h per feature, already included above.

findings.title: The auth boundary: public read-only pages, a single shared password, and writes only through Claude's OAuth token
findings.where: php/index.php:102-111 (TRACKER_PASSWORD required; DASHBOARD_PUBLIC default true), :157-161 (dashboardGuard), :218-219 (/mcp requires token), :271-272 (API requires token); php/lib/oauth.php:70-88 (require_token), :209-212 (single hash_equals password on consent); README.md lines 17, 36, 254; deploy.yml:25
findings.problem: Dashboards are readable by anyone with the link; every write requires a bearer token that only exists after the consent-screen password is entered by whoever configures the Claude connector. So a student-facing page can never accept input (tick a checklist item, 'I'm done', start a server-side timer) without either the student having her own connector on the same shared password, or a new unauthenticated POST path, which would be the first unauthenticated write in the service and undercuts 'TRACKER_PASSWORD is the only thing between the internet and the tracker'.
findings.why_it_matters: It decides the shape of features 4, 8 and 9: they must be read-only pages fed by tool calls made in the tutoring chat, not interactive apps. That is workable (the chat is where she already is) but it should be a decision, not a surprise mid-build. It also means the today page is visible to anyone who has the URL, which the family should knowingly accept or set DASHBOARD_PUBLIC=false and lose zero-friction access.
findings.proposal: Keep all student pages read-only and make the tutor skill the writer: the skill records 'started', flags, endings and checklist ticks through the tools. If interaction is ever wanted, the least-bad option is a per-page signed link (an HMAC of subject+action+day in the URL, checked in index.php) that permits exactly one idempotent write such as 'chunk finished', logged as a practice run with source 'student_page' (which would need adding to PRACTICE_SOURCE_SEED via a migration step and to the practice-test registry list). Document the choice in README 'Known limits'. Effort: 0 h now; about 4 h if signed links are wanted later.

findings.title: Everything is UTC, the family is in Europe/London: today, this-week and start-time features need a zone
findings.where: php/lib/mcp.php:1259 (session date defaults gmdate), :170, :179 (practice played_at converted to UTC); php/lib/practice.php:342 (7d window uses gmdate), :409-413 (board date is the first ten UTC characters); php/lib/store.php:919 (history since), :971-981 (weekOf at 12:00 UTC); php/lib/dashboard.php:180-183 (countdown from 09:00Z), :388 (footer 'UTC')
findings.problem: Every date is computed in UTC, which is correct for the audit trail but wrong for 'today' and 'this week' pages: on 2026-09-04 London is UTC+01:00, so a session or practice run at 00:30 BST is filed under the previous day, a 7d window boundary is off by an hour, and a started_at captured as 'now' would read an hour early. The countdown uses 09:00Z as the exam moment, which is fine.
findings.why_it_matters: A 'this week' figure that moves at 01:00 rather than midnight, or a session that appears on yesterday's date, is the kind of small wrongness that makes a student distrust the page; the whole value of a today page is that it agrees with the clock on the wall.
findings.proposal: Add const TRACKER_TZ = 'Europe/London' in store.php and a helper local_today(): string using DateTimeImmutable('now', new DateTimeZone(TRACKER_TZ)); use it for the default session date (mcp.php:1259), for started_at capture, for the today/week pages and the 'this week' ISO computation, while leaving played_at storage in UTC. Add one practice-test check that local_today() differs from gmdate('Y-m-d') at 23:30 UTC in July (freeze via a DateTimeImmutable argument rather than time()). Effort about 1.5 h; do it before finding 2.
